A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same angular-calibration and Platt-scaling work. All 24 pages of v2 and 26 pages of v4, including proofs, pseudocode, tables, figures, and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 7 and Appendix H report original simulations, Monte Carlo sign-estimation results, and semi-real calibration experiments using real covariates with simulated labels.

after.justification: The original empirical results remain, and Appendix H.3 adds ECE results and reliability diagrams for 20 further semi-real UCI/OpenML datasets.

M1.justification: The angular predictor, angle estimators, Algorithm 1, and multi-index extension in Appendix F are unchanged. The additional benchmarks do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Appendix H.3 expands real-covariate coverage from six to 26 datasets, adding sources such as HAR, MNIST, Covertype, SpeedDating, Diabetes-130US, and Appliances-Energy. The task remains binary calibration with simulated labels; the original datasets are retained.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 2 retain their comparator membership. Table 3 extends the same uncalibrated, Platt scaling, and isotonic regression comparisons, with the same 100/500-point calibration variants, to additional datasets.

E3.justification: The added suite introduces dataset-specific training, covariance-pool, and test allocations; for example, HAR uses 561 training, 8,038 covariance-pool, and 1,200 test observations. Existing experiments retain their settings, and the extension follows the established simulated-label, true-angle evaluation with ECE and 100/500-point baseline holdouts.

E4.justification: The controlled Rademacher/uniform and sigmoid/clipped-ReLU robustness experiments in Appendix H.1 are unchanged. H.3 extends benchmark ECE and reliability reporting without introducing a separate ablation, sensitivity, or mechanism analysis.

E5.justification: The reported 5,000 Monte Carlo sign-estimation trials are unchanged. The additional benchmark results use ECE point estimates without introducing repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Original simulation results and Tables 1–2 are unchanged. Table 3 adds 20 datasets and supports angular calibration having the lowest ECE on 15, with mean ECE 0.026 versus 0.049/0.034 for Platt 100/500. Some new baseline values disagree across displays: ada_agnostic uncalibrated ECE is 0.2000 in Table 3 but 0.2059 in Figure 6.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, formal results, and proofs in Sections 2–6 and Appendices A–F are unchanged after matching pagination and citation renumbering. The multi-index theorem and derivation were already present in v2.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central claims: provable high-dimensional calibration, Bregman optimality, and conditions guaranteeing Platt-scaling convergence. The additional experiments supply supporting evidence without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: H.3 interprets the new results as supporting calibration across varied feature types and explicitly identifies five datasets where angular calibration loses, describing the gaps as typically small. Existing qualifications about Gaussian assumptions, unstable angle estimation on real covariates, and using true angles remain unchanged.

D1.justification: H.3 adds dataset identifiers, feature descriptions, encoding information, and training/covariance/test sizes for the extended suite. These improve documentation of the new experiments; existing pseudocode, hyperparameters, and software information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds references to Dua and Graff's UCI repository and Vanschoren and colleagues' OpenML paper. These support dataset provenance; the positioning against prior calibration and high-dimensional inference research is otherwise unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 adds H.3, dataset descriptions, funding acknowledgments, and a brief pointer in Section 7.2. It also corrects two robustness-figure references, retitles H.2, and updates the conference footer. The existing exposition and section organization are largely unchanged.

P2.justification: The appendix substantially expands its visual comparisons through Table 3, including dataset/split columns, and the new 20-panel Figure 6. The earlier six-panel H.2 display becomes a captioned three-panel Figure 5: Communities & Crime, DNA, and Madelon plots are removed, although their Table 2 results remain. Figures 1–4 are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The broader semi-real evaluation tests calibration across more varied real covariates, documents dataset allocations, and discusses cases where alternatives win, modestly strengthening empirical support. It does not resolve the existing reliance on simulated labels and true angles. Table 3/Figure 6 baseline ECE discrepancies also limit the improvement in reporting quality.
